name: Migration runner
purpose: Owns the forward-only migration semantics. Reads the on-disk schema version, compares against the build's max known version, applies pending migrations in order inside one transaction each, and returns the version transition. Refuses to run when the on-disk version is newer than the build knows about. Rolls back and reports on any per-migration failure without attempting later migrations.
responsibilities: Ensure the bookkeeping table (schemaVersion with version PRIMARY KEY and appliedAt timestamp) exists idempotently before reading the on-disk version. This is the only DDL statement outside a versioned migration (AC-5102-3).

Read the on-disk highest version from the bookkeeping table. Compare against the max version in the loaded catalog. Throw a refuse-newer error with a stable code and a message naming both versions when the on-disk version is strictly greater (AC-5103-1, AC-5103-2).

For each pending migration in ascending order, open a transaction, execute every statement in the migration's statements list, insert the version bookkeeping row, and commit. On any failure, roll back and throw a migration-failed error naming the failing version and description; do not attempt later migrations (AC-5104-1, AC-5104-2, AC-5104-3, AC-5109-1).

Return a { from, to, applied } result carrying the pre-run highest version, the post-run highest version, and the array of versions applied during this run (empty on a no-op at target version) (AC-5106-2, AC-5111-1).
internalStructure: One migrate(engineHandle, catalog) function that reads the on-disk version, filters the catalog to pending entries, iterates them in order, and returns the transition record. Idempotent bookkeeping-table DDL runs once at entry. The transaction boundary is expressed in whatever primitive the engine binding provides (BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK for SQLite; BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK for Postgres). No state is retained between invocations.

interfaces.name: migrate
interfaces.description: migrate(engineHandle, catalog) -> { from, to, applied }; the sole entry point the store facade calls at open. Throws refuse-newer or migration-failed errors with stable codes on the failure paths.

dependencies.name: Migration catalog
dependencies.description: Consumed as the ordered list of pending migrations to apply. The catalog's max version anchors the refuse-newer comparison.

tradeoffs: Forward-only means no down migrations; a rollback to an older schema is a redeploy against the older code with the older catalog, and the newer store artifact refuses to open under the older build. That refusal is the safety property (see ADR-602); the cost is that a botched schema change is a code fix and a redeploy, not a schema-side undo. The runner holds no state, which means every open re-checks the on-disk version against the catalog and re-applies pending work idempotently on retry.
